theory.intro: A **Venn diagram** and a **two-way table** are two ways of showing how two attributes are connected. The rectangle $\xi$ around a Venn diagram holds everyone in the group: the overlap holds those with **both** attributes, and anything outside both circles has **neither**. A two-way table shows those same four groups as four cells, with a row of totals and a column of totals around them.
facts: The rectangle $\xi$ is the whole group surveyed, so the four regions — $A$ only, both, $B$ only and neither — add to the total.
The overlap is not the whole of $A$: if $17$ people are in $A$ and $6$ are in both, then $17 - 6 = 11$ are in $A$ only.
The four inner cells of a two-way table are the same four groups as the four regions of a Venn diagram.
Each row of a two-way table adds across to its row total and each column adds down to its column total; the two meet at the grand total in the corner.
A row or column total counts a whole attribute (everyone who studies Japanese), while a cell counts a combination (studies Japanese and plays netball) — never read one for the other.
A probability from either display is $\dfrac{\text{count in the region or cell}}{\text{total surveyed}}$, written as a fraction in simplest form.
steps: Subtract the overlap from each attribute total.
Use the fact that the four regions add to the group total.

foundation.solution_text:
a. The overlapping region shows $6$.
b. The region outside both circles shows $4$.
c. The Japanese-only region shows $11$.

foundation.question_text:
A group of Year 10 students was asked whether they study Music and whether they play basketball.
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Music}&\text{Not Music}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Basketball}&9&14&23\\\text{Not Basketball}&6&11&17\\\hline\text{Total}&15&25&40\end{array}$
How many students:
a. study Music and play basketball?
b. study Music?
c. were surveyed?
foundation.solution_text:
a. Read the cell where the Music column meets the Basketball row: $9$
b. Read the Music column total: $15$
c. Read the grand total in the corner: $40$

foundation.question_text:
Year 7 students were asked whether they study French and whether they play hockey.
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{French}&\text{Not French}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Hockey}&7&10&17\\\text{Not Hockey}&13&18&31\\\hline\text{Total}&20&28&48\end{array}$
How many students:
a. play hockey but do not study French?
b. do not play hockey?
c. do not study French?
foundation.solution_text:
a. Read the cell where the 'Not French' column meets the Hockey row: $10$
b. Read the 'Not Hockey' row total: $31$
c. Read the 'Not French' column total: $28$

foundation.question_text:
Copy and complete this two-way table for a Year 9 elective survey.
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Geography}&\text{Not Geography}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Commerce}&8&13&21\\\text{Not Commerce}&11&?&?\\\hline\text{Total}&19&25&44\end{array}$
foundation.solution_text:
The 'Not Geography' column must add down to its total.
$25 - 13$
$= 12$
The 'Not Commerce' row now adds across.
$11 + 12$
$= 23$

foundation.question_text:
A Year 8 sport survey recorded whether students play tennis and whether they swim in the school squad.
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Tennis}&\text{Not Tennis}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Swims}&9&15&24\\\text{Does not swim}&11&15&26\\\hline\text{Total}&20&30&50\end{array}$
One of these students is chosen at random. Find, as fractions in simplest form:
a. $P(\text{plays tennis and swims})$
b. $P(\text{swims})$

foundation.solution_text:
a. The overlapping region shows $0$.
b. $8 + 0 + 11$
$= 19$
c. The region outside both circles shows $41$.

The overlap becomes the Chinese–Soccer cell, and the region outside both circles becomes the 'Not Chinese, Not Soccer' cell.
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Chinese}&\text{Not Chinese}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Soccer}&5&9&14\\\text{Not Soccer}&7&4&11\\\hline\text{Total}&12&13&25\end{array}$

development.question_text: A survey of $60$ Year 10 students recorded whether they study Design and Technology and whether they play basketball. Altogether $25$ study Design and Technology, $32$ play basketball, and $14$ do both. Construct a two-way table for this data.
development.solution_text:
Basketball and Design and Technology: $14$
Basketball but not Design and Technology:
$32 - 14$
$= 18$
Design and Technology but not basketball:
$25 - 14$
$= 11$
Neither:
$60 - (11 + 14 + 18)$
$= 17$
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{D and T}&\text{Not D and T}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Basketball}&14&18&32\\\text{Not Basketball}&11&17&28\\\hline\text{Total}&25&35&60\end{array}$

development.question_text: A Year 8 cohort of $90$ students was surveyed about two electives. Altogether $36$ study Photography, and $12$ of those also study Coding. Of the students who do not study Photography, $40$ do not study Coding either. Construct a two-way table for this data.
development.solution_text:
Photography but not Coding:
$36 - 12$
$= 24$
Students who do not study Photography:
$90 - 36$
$= 54$
Of those, the ones who do study Coding:
$54 - 40$
$= 14$
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Photography}&\text{Not Photography}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Coding}&12&14&26\\\text{Not Coding}&24&40&64\\\hline\text{Total}&36&54&90\end{array}$

a. The overlap becomes the Commerce–Cricket cell.
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Commerce}&\text{Not Commerce}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Cricket}&8&17&25\\\text{Not Cricket}&13&6&19\\\hline\text{Total}&21&23&44\end{array}$
b. $\frac{8 + 17}{44}$
$= \frac{25}{44}$

development.question_text:
Copy and complete this two-way table, which records whether students study Music and whether they sing in the choir.
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Music}&\text{Not Music}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Choir}&?&9&22\\\text{Not Choir}&11&?&?\\\hline\text{Total}&24&?&50\end{array}$
development.solution_text:
The Choir row adds across to $22$.
$22 - 9$
$= 13$
The grand total gives the 'Not Choir' row total.
$50 - 22$
$= 28$
That row now adds across.
$28 - 11$
$= 17$
The 'Not Music' column total follows.
$9 + 17$
$= 26$

development.question_text:
This two-way table records whether Year 7 students study History and whether they play touch football.
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{History}&\text{Not History}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Touch}&15&21&36\\\text{Not Touch}&17&7&24\\\hline\text{Total}&32&28&60\end{array}$
One student is chosen at random. Find, as fractions in simplest form:
a. $P(\text{does not play touch football})$
b. $P(\text{studies History and plays touch football})$

mastery.question_text: $120$ Year 9 students were asked whether they study Italian. Two-thirds of those asked are girls. Altogether $26$ boys study Italian, and twice as many girls as boys do not study Italian. Use a two-way table to work out how many girls study Italian.
mastery.solution_text:
Girls:
$\frac{2}{3} \times 120$
$= 80$
Boys:
$120 - 80$
$= 40$
Boys who do not study Italian:
$40 - 26$
$= 14$
Girls who do not study Italian:
$2 \times 14$
$= 28$
Girls who study Italian:
$80 - 28$
$= 52$
$\begin{array}{l|cc|c}&\text{Italian}&\text{Not Italian}&\text{Total}\\\hline\text{Girls}&52&28&80\\\text{Boys}&26&14&40\\\hline\text{Total}&78&42&120\end{array}$
